briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East remains in a state of heightened conflict, primarily driven by extensive US military strikes against Iran and Iran's subsequent retaliatory attacks on US regional bases. The Strait of Hormuz is a major flashpoint, marked by alleged tanker attacks and conflicting claims over control, further exacerbating economic instability in Iran and global energy markets. Meanwhile, Israel continues military operations in Gaza, including the significant capture of a senior Hamas leader, and engages in cross-border exchanges with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran included widespread US airstrikes targeting various sites. In Sirik, Hormozgan province, a US strike reportedly hit a wedding ceremony, resulting in 5-18 fatalities and 68-109 injuries, including women and children, and destroying a telecom tower. Additional US strikes were reported in Jahrom, Fars province (killing a Basij bulldozer operator), Lavalan Island (killing 3 Basij members: Mehdi Bahrani, Hussein Saleh Nejad, Hassan Momeni), and Kermanshah (killing 4 IRGC air force personnel: Reza Mohammadi, Shahram Jaafari, Alireza Shakiba, Jaafar Kahrizi). Other targets included a military base in Bandar Abbas, port cities Chabahar and Qeshm (near the airport and a fish powder factory), a gas plant in Asaluyeh, a site near Ahvaz (7 military personnel killed), and the civilian airport radar in Jiroft. Iran's Health Ministry reported 18 killed and 108 injured nationwide from the attacks, with some sources claiming up to 21 fatalities. CENTCOM confirmed completing strikes against IRGC targets including air defense, radar, naval facilities, mine-laying capabilities, and communication centers, denying civilian targeting.

In retaliation, Iran launched missile and drone attacks. The IRGC claimed targeting US Marine base Camp Titin (Prince Hassan Air Base) in Jordan, destroying RQ-4 and MQ-9 drones and technical infrastructure, and claiming US casualties. Iran also claimed drone strikes on the US Fifth Fleet Headquarters/Sheikh Isa Base in Bahrain, and the Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait, destroying drone hangars and US commander's compounds. Furthermore, Iranian attacks reportedly hit a US military complex at Erbil International Airport in Iraq, targeting a balloon surveillance system and setting fuel tanks on fire.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical area of confrontation. The IRGC claimed two Iranian oil tankers, HAK and Sinopa, were hit by mines and set on fire after attempting to pass through an unauthorized route. UKMTO reported a security incident on August 31, involving a tanker with two casualties, which Saudi Arabia condemned as an attack on its tanker "Cedr." US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent denied Iran controls the Strait, stating 17 million barrels of oil passed through recently, and denied reports of mines. US President Trump claimed US control of the Strait, stating 28 ships were destroyed. Axios reported a new US "tanker for tanker" policy. Reuters indicated that Iranian oil exports have halted for seven weeks due to US naval blockades.

Internally, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf met with Hamas officials, emphasizing a "resistance front." Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned the US of a "new strategy" in war, diplomacy, and countering economic siege. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's plane was forced to land in Rasht due to activated air defenses in Tehran.

Economically, the Iranian Rial fell to an unprecedented 2.2 million to the US dollar (or 220,000-222,000 Toman). The Emami gold coin reached 224-226 million Toman. US officials stated Iran's economy is in "accelerated collapse," with only 30 million barrels of Iranian oil remaining on water. Daily gasoline consumption exceeded 148 million liters, attributed to US attacks on oil facilities and import difficulties. The stock market index dropped by 145,000 units.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included the demolition of a kilometer-long tunnel in the northern Gaza Strip by the Gaza Division's Northern Brigade and Yahalom unit, part of over 26 kilometers of tunnels destroyed since the October 2025 ceasefire. A significant operation led by the Shin Bet resulted in the capture of Muein al-Arabid, chief of Hamas's internal security apparatus, in Gaza City. Prime Minister Netanyahu visited Gaza, stating Israel controls 60% of the Strip and will not retreat, adding that intelligence would be gained from al-Arabid's capture. An Israeli strike killed two Hamas operatives, Talal Mustafa Saleh Badawi and Momen Saeed Mohammed Al-Hawari, accused of violating the ceasefire by advancing attacks and restoring Hamas capabilities.

On the home front, air defense sirens near Kiryat Shmona in northern Israel were triggered by a "suspicious aerial target" from Lebanon, but later declared a false alarm by the IDF. No casualties were reported from military operations.

Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu stated Iran would face severe consequences if it attacked Israel, asserting Israel's capability to "defeat" and "overthrow" the Iranian regime. Defense Minister Israel Katz warned of potential Iranian attacks during Jewish holidays due to economic pressure. The Security Cabinet is scheduled to convene on Sunday evening. Attorney General is expected to approve a fuel price reduction despite it being an election period. MK Moshe Feiglin advocated for a swift victory in Gaza without leaving any Gazans. MK Rabbi Yitzhak Goldknopf called for leniency and release of Haredi draft dodgers for Jewish holidays, a sentiment echoed by Chief Rabbi Kalman Bar regarding Givati soldiers who refused to ride with a female paramedic. Ofer Winter, leader of "Amcha Israel," stated he would only form coalitions with "new people" not associated with October 7 and would not join a government without a law ending draft dodging, also insisting on integrating Haredim into the IDF.

Civilian impact included a fire near Ramat Gan stadium causing train delays, a double murder in Nazareth, and a fatal hit-and-run in Tel Aviv. Ultra-Orthodox extremists protested at the home of police traffic division head over the arrest of Haredi draft dodgers. A program to shield northern communities was launched. Water supply to farmers in the South was restored after disruptions.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations in Gaza included the demolition of a kilometer-long tunnel by the IDF's Northern Brigade and Yahalom unit in the northern Gaza Strip. The IDF claims over 26 kilometers of tunnels have been destroyed since the October 2025 ceasefire. Artillery fire was directed by the IDF towards buildings near Kuwait Junction in Gaza City's Zaytoun neighborhood, and airstrikes in eastern Gaza City reportedly hit the Baptist Hospital complex. Following the capture of Hamas's internal security chief, Israel increased its alert level on the Gaza border, with increased helicopter activity and fire in northern Gaza.

In terms of casualties, an Israeli strike killed Talal Mustafa Saleh Badawi, a commander in Hamas's military security department in Gaza City Brigade, and Momen Saeed Mohammed Al-Hawari, another Hamas operative, for "systematic violation of the ceasefire." A suspected Israeli drone strike hit a tent for displaced persons in Mawasi, Khan Younis, injuring five people.

The humanitarian situation remains precarious, highlighted by the strike on a displaced persons' tent.

Regarding ceasefire status, Israel justified killing Hamas operatives by stating they were systematically violating the ceasefire. The capture of Muein al-Arabid, Hamas's chief of internal security, was a significant event, with Israel's President Herzog noting al-Arabid had sought to prevent Hamas's disarmament. Hamas's platform "Al-Majd" issued emergency instructions to its operatives, urging avoidance of mobile phones and caution in movement, fearing further arrests.

In the West Bank (Judea and Samaria), President Herzog noted significant state efforts to thwart violence and bring perpetrators to justice.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched two explosive-laden drones overnight at Israeli troops operating at Ali Taher Ridge in southern Lebanon; one was shot down, and no Israeli soldiers were injured. In response, Israel's military conducted strikes against Hezbollah infrastructure in the Nabatieh area, which the IDF stated were used for planning and directing terror attacks. Israeli fighter jets also targeted Nabatieh al-Fawqa. Further Israeli strikes were reported in Al-Qantara, Houla, Al-Mansouri, Arnon al-Shaqif, Mays al-Jabal, and Kafr Tebnit in southern Lebanon.

An initial report of a hostile drone crossing from Lebanon into Israeli territory triggered sirens near Kiryat Shmona, with interceptor missiles launched. However, the IDF later declared it a "false identification" and a false alarm.

US sources reported an investigation into an Iranian network using forged Lebanese documents of deceased citizens to facilitate movement for IRGC personnel via Beirut airport and land crossings, with suspected involvement of Hezbollah in death record irregularities and Lebanese General Security in passport issuance.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Iraq, Sheikh Akram al-Kaabi, Secretary-General of Harakat al-Nujaba, issued a strong warning that if any US soldiers remain in Iraq after September 30, their bodies would be returned.

Iran claimed missile and drone attacks on US military positions at Erbil International Airport, Iraq. Satellite images reportedly show a large charred area at a US military complex there, indicating the targeting of a balloon surveillance system and setting fuel tanks on fire. Separately, a massive fire broke out at the Khabat Power Plant in Erbil.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) reported resolving questions regarding Syria's past nuclear activities but noted no progress on Iran's nuclear file.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's national shipping company reported two Filipino crew members were killed after their ship was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. Saudi Arabia officially condemned the targeting of its tanker "Cedr." The US Embassy in Saudi Arabia warned American citizens in the Middle East to exercise increased vigilance due to regional tensions. An American official, cited by Al Arabiya, stated that US strikes against Iran were preemptive, targeting an Iranian plan to damage undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz.

The UAE was reportedly targeted by Iranian drone strikes on US radar systems and troop positions at Al Dhafra and Al Minhad bases. A US helicopter distress call was reported over the UAE.

Qatar shut down two air corridors over its airspace and is reportedly mediating between the US and Iran.

Kuwait reported its air defenses were confronting hostile drone attacks, which it attributed to "sinful Iranian aggression." Explosions were heard, and flight arrivals to Kuwait were halted due to Iranian air attacks. Iran claimed drone strikes on the US Ali Al-Salem Air Base, hitting the commander's compound and drone hangars.

Bahrain also reported explosions and active air defenses. Iran claimed drone strikes on the US Fifth Fleet Headquarters (Sheikh Isa base). Iran warned it would no longer "hold back" towards Bahrain and Kuwait.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent advised Gulf states to "stay away from Iran."

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Extensive US Strikes in Iran:** The US conducted widespread strikes in southern and western Iran, hitting military sites, infrastructure (e.g., telecom tower in Sirik, Jiroft airport radar), and reportedly a wedding ceremony in Sirik, Hormozgan province, leading to 5-18 fatalities and 68-109 injuries, including women and children.
2.  **Iranian Retaliatory Attacks:** Iran launched missile and drone attacks against US military bases in Jordan (Prince Hassan Air Base), Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Base), Kuwait (Ali Al-Salem Air Base), UAE (Al Dhafra and Al Minhad), and Iraq (Erbil International Airport). Kuwait confirmed confronting hostile drone attacks, and Jordan intercepted 10 of 13 incoming Iranian missiles.
3.  **Strait of Hormuz Escalation:** The IRGC claimed two Iranian oil tankers, HAK and Sinopa, were hit by mines and set ablaze. This followed a previous attack on a Saudi tanker, "Cedr." The US implemented a "tanker for tanker" policy, with US President Trump claiming control of the Strait and destroying 28 ships, while the US Treasury Secretary denied Iranian control and reports of mines.
4.  **Hamas Security Chief Captured:** Israeli special forces, in cooperation with the Shin Bet, captured Muein al-Arabid, the chief of Hamas's internal security apparatus, in Gaza City.
5.  **Hezbollah-Israel Cross-Border Engagements:** Hezbollah launched two explosive-laden drones at Israeli troops in southern Lebanon (Ali Taher Ridge), with one being intercepted. Israel retaliated with strikes against Hezbollah infrastructure in Nabatieh and other southern Lebanese towns.
6.  **Severe Iranian Economic Deterioration:** The Iranian Rial plummeted to an unprecedented low of 2.2 million per US dollar. US officials stated Iranian oil exports have halted for seven weeks due to blockades, and only 30 million barrels of Iranian oil remain on water, contributing to significant inflation concerns.
7.  **Russia's Covert Military Aid to Iran:** Reports indicate Russia has secretly assisted Iran in developing advanced supersonic cruise missiles since 2023, providing engineers and technical reports, with this cooperation continuing into 2026.
8.  **Jordanian Leadership Change:** King Abdullah of Jordan appointed Major General Majdi Al-Harasis as the new Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, hours after Jordan intercepted 10 out of 13 Iranian missiles.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high following direct US-Iran military exchanges. The US has threatened more severe actions, including the "complete destruction" of Iran as a country, if Iran retaliates further, while Iran's SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned of a "new strategy." Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where maritime attacks and conflicting claims of control persist, and US military bases across the Gulf, Jordan, and Iraq, which remain targets for Iranian retaliatory strikes. The Israeli-Lebanese border is another flashpoint, marked by ongoing Hezbollah-Israel exchanges. Military postures indicate increased readiness, with US forces described as "vigilant, deadly, and ready," Iranian air defenses active, and Jordan making leadership changes to enhance air defense capabilities. Minister of Defense Israel Katz warned of potential Iranian attacks during Jewish holidays. Red lines appear blurred, with the US denying targeting civilians while a wedding ceremony was reportedly hit, prompting Iran to condemn the act as a "war crime."

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** stance is assertive. Secretary of State Marco Rubio affirmed continued targeting of Iran over shipping attacks and urged international partners to cease business with the Nicaraguan government, also stating the US would sanction countries aiding Iran's revenue generation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described Iran's economy as in "accelerated collapse," aiming for negotiations on Trump's terms, and denied Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump, while denying he sought negotiations, claimed US control of the Strait, warned of Iran's "complete destruction" if it escalates, and urged the Iranian people to "rise up." CENTCOM confirmed its strikes on IRGC targets and denied targeting civilians in Sirik.

Among **Gulf States**, Saudi Arabia's national shipping company reported casualties from an attack in the Strait of Hormuz and officially condemned it, while the US Embassy warned American citizens in the Middle East to be vigilant. Kuwait publicly confirmed confronting hostile Iranian drone attacks, with air defenses active and flight arrivals halted. Qatar has shut two air corridors and is reportedly engaged in mediation efforts. US pressure on Gulf states includes calls from Treasury Secretary Bessent to "stay away from Iran."

**EU members** have also reacted. Germany successfully tested an Israeli-made LORA ballistic missile and officially blamed Russia for a drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport, implementing countermeasures including closing the Russian consulate in Bonn and restricting Russian diplomats' movement. Germany rejected invoking NATO's Article 4. In Belgium, a defense factory owned by Elbit Systems was set on fire by pro-Palestine activists.

**Russia** has reportedly provided covert assistance to Iran since 2023 in developing supersonic cruise missiles, continuing into 2026. Deputy Security Council Head Dmitry Medvedev threatened Germany with a "direct strike" on its arms factories for supplying Ukraine.

**China**, through President Xi Jinping, called for an end to "external intervention" and "double standards" in the Middle East during a visit to Egypt. Notably, China rejected a G20 statement supporting freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Unconfirmed reports suggested China set conditions for Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalibaf's visit, including reopening Hormuz and resolving issues with Saudi Arabia and the US.

**Turkey** President Erdogan stated that exploring Shanghai Cooperation Organization membership does not indicate a shift away from the West.

**Jordan** appointed a new Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Major General Majdi Al-Harasis, following the interception of 10 of 13 Iranian missiles fired into its airspace.

**Peru** severed diplomatic relations with Iran, citing concerns over "deterioration of democracy protection in Iran, closure of Strait of Hormuz, encouraging violence in ME, hindering IAEA work."

The **UN** Secretary-General expressed concern over US attacks in Iran, and the Iranian Red Crescent called for the ICC to investigate the Sirik wedding attack.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist within the reporting. Casualty figures from the Sirik wedding attack vary widely, from 5-18 killed and 68-109 injured (N12, Mamlekate, PressTV) to claims of 21 fatalities including children (PressTV Gisoo Ahmadi). US officials reported no casualties from Iranian attacks in Jordan, directly contradicting IRGC claims of American forces killed or injured in Jordan and Iraq. There are conflicting accounts regarding control and incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, with President Trump claiming US control and destruction of 28 ships, while US Treasury Secretary Bessent denied Iranian control and reports of mine incidents involving two tankers (which the IRGC claimed to have attacked). Trump's and Bessent's statements also diverge on whether the US seeks negotiations with Iran.

Unverified claims include the extent of damage and specific equipment destroyed in Iranian retaliatory strikes on US bases, the alleged failure of 3 out of 11 Iranian missiles, and the Russian assistance to Iran in developing hypersonic missiles (reported by Financial Times). Claims by Iranian hackers of unsuccessful attacks on US infrastructure also remain unverified.

Propaganda indicators are evident from both sides. Iranian rhetoric labels the US as "Satan" and accuses it of "war crimes" for the wedding attack. US rhetoric, particularly from President Trump, involves strong warnings of Iran's destruction and calls for the Iranian people to "rise up." CENTCOM denied civilian targeting despite reports of a wedding hit.

Reporting gaps include a precise, independently verifiable timeline and comprehensive details of all US strikes in Iran, particularly concerning civilian casualties and infrastructure damage. Similar gaps exist for the full scope of damage and casualties from Iranian retaliatory strikes on US bases. The exact nature of the UKMTO reported security incident in the Strait of Hormuz and the involved vessels requires further clarity.
